## Task
Implement Sprint 1: Demo Ticket Catalog & Reset Infrastructure

## Branch
Create and switch to branch: `ai/sprint-1-demo-ticket-catalog-reset-infrastructure`
Run: `git checkout -b ai/sprint-1-demo-ticket-catalog-reset-infrastructure` (or `git checkout ai/sprint-1-demo-ticket-catalog-reset-infrastructure` if it already exists from a retry)

## Sprint Specification
{
  "sprint_number": 1,
  "name": "Demo Ticket Catalog & Reset Infrastructure",
  "goal": "Create a rich, diverse set of pre-loaded demo tickets and a bulletproof one-click reset that restores the full demo state.",
  "features": [
    {
      "id": "s1-f1",
      "name": "Expanded Demo Ticket Suite",
      "description": "Extend the seed data with 8\u201310 new tickets across three properties that represent the full spectrum of agent capabilities. Tickets should include: (1) Vendor coordination tickets \u2014 e.g., broken boiler needing HVAC dispatch, plumbing leak requiring emergency scheduling, intercom replacement quote request. (2) Tenant inquiry tickets \u2014 e.g., a tenant asking about recycling rules via email, a tenant calling about a lost package, a tenant messaging about guest parking policy. (3) Owner financial action tickets \u2014 e.g., monthly cost summary request from an owner, invoice forwarding after a completed job, rent arrears notification to an owner. Each ticket should arrive from a different source (phone, email, letter, portal) so the multi-channel nature is visible. All tickets start in 'new' or 'triaged' status so the agent has work to do.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "At least 3 tickets require vendor email coordination as their resolution path",
        "At least 3 tickets represent tenant questions from different channels (phone, email, portal)",
        "At least 2 tickets require sending financial information to property owners",
        "At least 1 ticket is designed to trigger a human escalation (e.g., legal concern, high-cost decision above threshold)",
        "Each ticket has realistic German-language content (subject, excerpt, raised-by details) consistent with the existing seed style",
        "All new tickets reference existing properties, units, tenants, and vendors from seed data"
      ],
      "touches": [
        "seed service",
        "ticket templates"
      ],
      "risk_notes": "Must not break the existing 3 demo tickets (t-7831, t-7832, t-7833) \u2014 extend, don't replace."
    },
    {
      "id": "s1-f2",
      "name": "Context Enrichment for Agent Decision-Making",
      "description": "Enrich the property context files and policy rules so the Hermes agent has enough information to autonomously resolve each demo ticket type. Add vendor email addresses and communication preferences to the vendor layer. Add tenant communication preferences and FAQ answers to the property layer (e.g., recycling rules, parking policy, package handling). Add owner financial reporting preferences (format, frequency, preferred channel) to the owner layer. Add escalation rules that clearly define when the agent must defer to a human.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "Vendor context includes email addresses and preferred communication method for each vendor",
        "Property context includes answers to the common tenant questions seeded in the tickets",
        "Owner context includes financial reporting preferences (at least email and format)",
        "Escalation policies are explicit \u2014 at least one rule triggers human escalation for the demo",
        "Context is seeded as part of the reset flow so it's always available"
      ],
      "touches": [
        "seed service",
        "context versions",
        "property policies"
      ],
      "risk_notes": "Context changes affect the 4-layer markdown format \u2014 must maintain layer separation (vendor/owner/building/property)."
    },
    {
      "id": "s1-f3",
      "name": "One-Click Demo Reset Button",
      "description": "Add a prominent 'Reset Demo' button to the UI that calls the existing /dev/reset endpoint and restores the entire platform to its initial demo state. After reset, all tickets return to their starting statuses, all proposals and vendor jobs are cleared, all context versions revert to seed state, and audit logs are wiped. The button should show a confirmation dialog, then a loading state while reset runs, and finally redirect to the overview page with a success toast.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "A clearly visible 'Reset Demo' button exists in the UI (e.g., in the sidebar or top nav)",
        "Clicking it shows a confirmation dialog warning that all progress will be lost",
        "After confirmation, the full database is wiped and re-seeded with all demo data",
        "The UI redirects to the overview page and shows a success notification",
        "The reset completes in under 5 seconds",
        "After reset, all new demo tickets appear in 'new' or 'triaged' status, ready for the agent"
      ],
      "touches": [
        "frontend sidebar/nav",
        "dev routes",
        "seed service"
      ],
      "risk_notes": "The existing /dev/reset endpoint drops all tables \u2014 verify it handles the new seed data and any new models added in later sprints."
    },
    {
      "id": "s1-f4",
      "name": "Demo Mode Indicator",
      "description": "Add a visual indicator in the UI that shows the platform is in 'demo mode' \u2014 a subtle banner or badge that communicates this is a showcase environment. This sets audience expectations and makes the two control buttons (toggle agent, reset) feel intentional rather than accidental.",
      "acceptance_criteria": [
        "A 'Demo Mode' badge or banner is visible on all pages",
        "It does not interfere with normal platform usage or obstruct content",
        "It visually groups with the toggle agent and reset buttons"
      ],
      "touches": [
        "frontend layout/nav"
      ],
      "risk_notes": null
    }
  ],
  "success_criteria": [
    "After running reset, the overview page shows 8+ tickets in early pipeline stages (new/triaged)",
    "Tickets span all three action categories: vendor coordination, tenant response, owner financials",
    "The platform context contains enough information for the agent to resolve each ticket type",
    "The reset button reliably returns the demo to a clean starting state every time"
  ]
}

## Full Spec Constraints
[
  "The existing Hermes agent uses Google Gemini 2.5 Flash via OpenRouter \u2014 all new agent actions must work through this same LLM gateway",
  "Write tools follow the proposal-envelope pattern \u2014 they propose actions for human confirmation, never execute directly",
  "The SSE streaming infrastructure already exists in the chat engine \u2014 reuse it for action streaming rather than building a parallel system",
  "The seed service must remain idempotent \u2014 safe to run multiple times without duplicating data",
  "The frontend is a Next.js 15 app in a pnpm monorepo with shadcn/ui components \u2014 all new UI must use this stack",
  "The backend uses SQLAlchemy with Alembic migrations and PostgreSQL \u2014 new models require proper migrations",
  "All API responses must follow the existing standardized format with camelCase serialization",
  "The existing /dev/reset endpoint drops all tables \u2014 it must be extended to handle any new models/tables",
  "Context files use a 4-layer markdown format (vendor/owner/building/property) \u2014 additions must respect this structure",
  "The agent has a 50-turn budget per invocation (HERMES_MAX_TURNS) \u2014 batch processing must manage this per-ticket"
]

## Out of Scope
[
  "Actually sending real emails, SMS, or messages to external systems \u2014 all actions are simulated/displayed in the UI",
  "Multi-user authentication or role-based access \u2014 this is a single-presenter demo environment",
  "Production deployment or scaling \u2014 this runs locally or on a single demo instance",
  "Modifying the core Hermes agent LLM or switching providers",
  "Mobile responsiveness \u2014 the demo targets a laptop/projector presentation setup",
  "Internationalization beyond the existing German ticket content",
  "Integration with real Slack, email, or SMS providers",
  "Persistent demo state across server restarts \u2014 reset is expected after restart"
]

## Instructions
1. Read CLAUDE.md and key source files to understand current patterns
2. Create the branch
3. Implement each feature in the order listed
4. Commit after each feature with format: [ai-builder/generator] description\nSprint: 1 | Feature: <id>
5. After ALL features are implemented, output the sprint contract as a ```json block

Set branch to "ai/sprint-1-demo-ticket-catalog-reset-infrastructure" in the contract.

Perfect! Now I have a comprehensive understanding of the repository. Let me create a summary document with all the findings.

## Repository Exploration Summary: Hermes Property Management Platform

I've thoroughly explored the Hermes repository. Here's the complete breakdown:

### 1. OVERALL DIRECTORY STRUCTURE

**Root projects:**
- `/backend` - FastAPI + SQLAlchemy Python backend
- `/frontend` - Next.js 15 monorepo (pnpm workspace)
- `/data` - Property data files (stammdaten, rechnungen, briefe, emails, etc.)
- `/docs` - Documentation
- `/hermes` - Appears to be an upstream/reference implementation

### 2. BACKEND STRUCTURE

**Tech Stack:**
- Framework: FastAPI 0.111.0
- ORM: SQLAlchemy 2.0.30
- Database: PostgreSQL 16
- Async: asyncpg 0.29.0

**Key Files:**
- `/backend/app/main.py` - FastAPI app with CORS middleware, error handlers, route registration
- `/backend/app/database.py` - SQLAlchemy session management
- `/backend/requirements.txt` - Python dependencies
- `/backend/run.py` - Application runner
- `/backend/alembic/` - Database migrations (5 versions)

**API Routes** (`/backend/app/api/routes/`):
- `dev.py` - Development endpoints including **`POST /dev/reset`** and `/dev/simulate-ticket`
- `tickets.py` - Ticket CRUD and actions
- `properties.py` - Property management
- `context.py` - Property context versions
- `policies.py` - Policy evaluation
- `proposals.py` - Agent proposals
- `messages.py` - Owner messages
- `attachments.py` - File uploads
- `documents.py` - Property documents
- `owners.py`, `buildings.py`, `vendors.py`, `units.py` - Knowledge layer
- `audit.py` - Audit trail
- `escalations.py` - Escalated tickets
- `chat.py` - Chat/messaging
- `extract.py` - PDF extraction

**Models** (`/backend/app/models/`):
All 20+ models with stable IDs:
```
- properties.py          (p1, p2, p3)
- buildings.py           (b1, b2, b3)
- owners.py              (o1, o2)
- vendors.py             (v1, v2, v3, v4)
- units.py               (u-1a...u-5a, u-e1)
- tickets.py             (t-7831, t-7832, t-7833)
- agent_proposals.py     (pr-7831)
- call_sessions.py       (cs-7831)
- vendor_jobs.py         (vj-7832)
- context_versions.py
- context_chunks.py
- context_sources.py
- property_policies.py
- property_ticket_counters.py
- vendor_cases.py        (vc1, vc2, vc3)
- owner_messages.py
- attachments.py
- audit_log.py
- extractions.py
- property_documents.py
- building_vendors.py
```

**Services** (`/backend/app/services/`):
- `seed_service.py` - **Database seeding with 4-layer context markdown**
- `ticket_pipeline.py` - Core orchestration
- `proposal_engine.py` - AI proposal generation
- `policy_evaluator.py` - Policy rule evaluation
- `context_service.py` - Property context loading
- `context_layer_service.py` - Layer-specific context handling
- `audit_service.py` - Immutable audit trail
- `slack_service.py` - Slack notifications
- `ticket_number_service.py` - Auto-numbering (GAR-118, etc)
- `vendor_job_service.py` - Vendor job lifecycle
- `agent_runtime.py`, `agent_tools.py` - Agent execution
- Others for chat, extraction, memory, etc.

**Ticket Structure** (10-state lifecycle):
```python
VALID_TICKET_STATUSES = {
    "new", "triaged", "proposed", "approved", 
    "awaiting_vendor", "scheduled", "in_progress", 
    "completed", "resolved", "rejected"
}
```

### 3. DEMO TICKETS (STABLE IDs)

**File:** `/backend/app/services/seed_service.py` (lines 486-545)

```
t-7831: "Heating cold — Unit 3B"
  - Status: proposed
  - Source: voice
  - Raised by: Herr Schmidt
  - Num: GAR-118
  - Risk: medium (confidence 0.86)
  - Proposal: pr-7831 (dispatch Heinz GmbH, €175)
  - Call session: cs-7831 (German/English transcript)

t-7832: "Intercom not working — Unit E1"
  - Status: completed
  - Source: email
  - Raised by: Café Krone
  - Num: GAR-119
  - Risk: low (confidence 0.91)
  - Vendor job: vj-7832 (Bekey Service, €90, completed)

t-7833: "Noise complaint — Unit 3A"
  - Status: triaged
  - Source: manual
  - Raised by: Familie Torres
  - Num: GAR-120
  - Risk: low
  - Unit: u-2b
```

### 4. CONTEXT FILES - 4-LAYER MARKDOWN FORMAT

**File:** `/backend/app/services/seed_service.py` (lines 44-150)

Each property's `context.md` has 4 sections with `## Layer` headings:

```markdown
---
version: 11
updated_at: 2026-04-20
updated_by: memory-agent
---

## Vendor layer
**Preferred vendors:**
- Heinz GmbH (HVAC, SLA 24h) — v1
- Bekey Service (Access/Intercom, SLA 48h) — v2
...

## Owner layer
**WEG Gartenstraße 42** (WEG) — contact: Herr Klein
- Email, phone, policies, decisions...

## Building layer
**Gartenstraße 42** — Altbau 1928, 8 units
- HVAC, heating, elevator, intercom systems...

## Property layer
**Address**: Gartenstraße 42, 10115 Berlin
**Phone/Email/Units/City**
### Units & Tenants
### Recent Decisions
```

**Demo contexts:**
- `GARTENSTR_CONTEXT` (p1) - v11, 8 units, WEG owner, Heinz/Bekey/Schmidt vendors
- `BRUNNENSTR_CONTEXT` (p2) - v3, 6 units, Klaus Weber (private)
- `LINIENSTR_CONTEXT` (p3) - v5, 5 units, Ingrid Sommer (private)

### 5. RESET ENDPOINT

**File:** `/backend/app/api/routes/dev.py` (lines 40-71)

```python
@router.post("/dev/reset")
def reset_database(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    """
    Drop all data and re-seed the database with the full demo dataset.
    WARNING: Destructive operation — for dev/demo use only.
    Idempotent: calling reset twice produces the same state.
    """
    # Deletes all tables in FK dependency order
    # Then calls run_seed(db)
    return {"message": "Database reset and re-seeded", "seed_result": result}
```

**Additional dev endpoints:**
- `POST /dev/simulate-ticket` - Create ticket from template
- `GET /dev/ticket-templates` - List available templates
- `POST /dev/complete-vendor-job/{job_id}` - Mark vendor job complete

### 6. FRONTEND STRUCTURE

**Tech Stack:**
- Framework: Next.js 15 (App Router)
- UI Library: shadcn/ui components
- Styling: Tailwind CSS 4.0
- Icons: Lucide React 0.453.0
- Package Manager: pnpm 9.0.0

**Main Layout:** `/frontend/apps/web/app/layout.tsx`
- Root wrapper with Sidebar, Toaster, ThemeProvider

**Sidebar Component:** `/frontend/apps/web/components/sidebar.tsx`
- Collapsible sidebar with navigation
- Work zone: Overview, Escalations
- Properties zone: Expandable property list (p1, p2, p3) with tabs
- Knowledge zone: Vendors, Owners, Buildings
- Tools zone: PDF Extract, Hermes Chat
- Footer: Theme toggle, context.md version, Hermes status
- **No reset button in sidebar** - would need to be added

**Pages/Routes:**
```
/overview                      - Dashboard (KPIs, pipeline stages)
/property/[id]/
  - tickets                    - Ticket list for property
  - units                      - Units & owners
  - context                    - Read-only 4-layer view
  - editor                     - Context editor
  - versions                   - Version history
  - sources                    - Knowledge sources
  - policies                   - Policies
  - calls                       - Call sessions
/ticket/[id]                   - Ticket detail (approval/rejection/memory decisions)
/owners                        - Owner list
/owner/[id]                    - Owner detail
/buildings                     - Building list
/building/[id]                 - Building detail
/vendors                       - Vendor list
/vendor/[id]                   - Vendor detail
/escalations                   - Escalated tickets
/extract                       - PDF extraction tool
/chat                          - Chat interface
```

**API Client:** `/frontend/apps/web/lib/api.ts`
- `api.properties.list()` - GET /api/properties
- `api.tickets.{list, get, approve, reject, saveMemory, skipMemory}`
- `api.context.{get, versions, specific}`
- `api.owners.{list, get}`
- `api.buildings.{list, get}`
- `api.vendors.{list, get}`
- **No dev/reset endpoint exposed yet**

**Types:** `/frontend/apps/web/lib/types.ts`
```typescript
interface Property {
  id, name, buildingId, ownerId, city, units, openTickets, contextVersion, phone, email
}

interface Ticket {
  id, num, propertyId, unitId, source, status, risk, subject, excerpt, raisedBy, 
  raisedByPhone, createdAt, confidence, proposal, callSession, vendorJob, memoryProposal
```
}

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from sqlalchemy import text
from typing import List

from app.database import get_db
from app.models import (
    Property, ContextVersion, ContextChunk, PropertyPolicy, ContextSource,
    Ticket, AgentProposal, AuditLog, OwnerMessage, Attachment,
)
from app.models.properties import Property as PropertyModel
from app.models.owners import Owner
from app.models.buildings import Building
from app.models.building_vendors import BuildingVendor
from app.models.vendors import Vendor
from app.models.vendor_cases import VendorCase
from app.models.units import Unit
from app.models.call_sessions import CallSession
from app.models.vendor_jobs import VendorJob
from app.models.extractions import Extraction
from app.models.property_ticket_counters import PropertyTicketCounter
from app.schemas.tickets import TicketOut, VendorJobOut
from app.seed import TICKET_TEMPLATES, run_seed
from app.services.audit_service import create_audit_entry
from app.services import vendor_job_service

router = APIRouter()


class SimulateTicketRequest(BaseModel):
    template_id: str


class CompleteVendorJobRequest(BaseModel):
    final_cost_eur: float | None = None
    notes: str | None = None


@router.post("/dev/reset")
def reset_database(db: Session = Depends(get_db)):
    """
    Drop all data and re-seed the database with the full demo dataset.
    WARNING: Destructive operation — for dev/demo use only.
    Idempotent: calling reset twice produces the same state.
    """
    # Delete in reverse FK dependency order
    db.query(AuditLog).delete()
    db.query(Attachment).delete()
    db.query(OwnerMessage).delete()
    db.query(VendorJob).delete()
    db.query(CallSession).delete()
    db.query(Extraction).delete()
    db.query(PropertyTicketCounter).delete()
    db.query(AgentProposal).delete()
    db.query(Ticket).delete()
    db.query(Unit).delete()
    db.query(ContextSource).delete()
    db.query(PropertyPolicy).delete()
    db.query(ContextChunk).delete()
    db.query(ContextVersion).delete()
    db.query(VendorCase).delete()
    db.query(BuildingVendor).delete()
    db.query(Property).delete()
    db.query(Building).delete()
    db.query(Vendor).delete()
    db.query(Owner).delete()
    db.commit()

    result = run_seed(db)
    return {"message": "Database reset and re-seeded", "seed_result": result}


@router.post("/dev/simulate-ticket", response_model=TicketOut, status_code=201)
def simulate_ticket(
    request: SimulateTicketRequest,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Create a ticket from a predefined template."""
    template = next((t for t in TICKET_TEMPLATES if t["id"] == request.template_id), None)
    if not template:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=404,
            detail=f"Template '{request.template_id}' not found. Available: {[t['id'] for t in TICKET_TEMPLATES]}",
        )

    # Find property by name
    prop = (
        db.query(PropertyModel)
        .filter(PropertyModel.name == template["property"])
        .first()
    )
    if not prop:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=422,
            detail=f"Property '{template['property']}' not found in database. Run /dev/reset first.",
        )

    # Auto-generate ticket number
    ticket_num = None
    try:
        from app.services.ticket_number_service import next_ticket_num
        ticket_num = next_ticket_num(db, prop.id)
    except Exception:
        pass

    from app.models.tickets import Ticket
    ticket = Ticket(
        property_id=prop.id,
        source=template["source"],
        raised_by=template["raised_by"],
        subject=template["subject"],
        body=template["body"],
        status="new",
        num=ticket_num,
    )
    db.add(ticket)
    db.flush()

    create_audit_entry(
        db,
        actor="dev-simulator",
        action="ticket.create",
        entity_type="ticket",
        property_id=prop.id,
        entity_id=ticket.id,
        metadata={"template_id": template["id"], "template_name": template["name"]},
    )
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(ticket)

    # Trigger the proposal pipeline
    try:
        from app.services.ticket_pipeline import run_pipeline
        run_pipeline(ticket.id, db)
        db.refresh(ticket)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"[pipeline] Warning: pipeline failed for ticket {ticket.id}: {e}")

    return ticket


@router.get("/dev/ticket-templates")
def list_ticket_templates():
    """List all available ticket simulation templates."""
    return {"templates": TICKET_TEMPLATES}


@router.post("/dev/complete-vendor-job/{job_id}", response_model=VendorJobOut)
def dev_complete_vendor_job(
    job_id: str,
    payload: CompleteVendorJobRequest | None = None,
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """
    Mark a vendor job complete (lifecycle terminal state). Mirrors the ticket
    to 'completed' and runs the memory engine to fill the proposal's
    final_context_update_md so the operator's memory decision becomes visible.

    Dev-only shortcut for the demo flow — production would receive this via
    a vendor webhook.
    """
    cost = payload.final_cost_eur if payload else None
    notes = payload.notes if payload else None
    job = vendor_job_service.complete(db, job_id, final_cost_eur=cost, notes=notes)
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(job)
    return job


@router.post("/dev/test-conflict")
def dev_test_conflict():
    """Force-trigger the StateConflictError handler (for envelope tests)."""
    from app.exceptions import StateConflictError
    raise StateConflictError("Synthetic conflict for envelope testing")

import sqlalchemy as sa
from app.database import Base

# 10-state ticket status (app-layer string enum, NOT a Postgres ENUM type
# so that adding new states never requires a DB migration)
VALID_TICKET_STATUSES = {
    "new",
    "triaged",
    "proposed",
    "approved",
    "awaiting_vendor",
    "scheduled",
    "in_progress",
    "completed",
    "resolved",
    "rejected",
}


class Ticket(Base):
    __tablename__ = "tickets"

    id = sa.Column(
        sa.String,
        primary_key=True,
        server_default=sa.text("gen_random_uuid()"),
    )
    property_id = sa.Column(
        sa.String,
        sa.ForeignKey("properties.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
    )
    source = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)
    external_id = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=True)
    raised_by = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)

    # Sprint-1 extensions
    num = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=True)           # e.g. "GAR-118"
    unit_id = sa.Column(
        sa.String,
        sa.ForeignKey("units.id", ondelete="SET NULL"),
        nullable=True,
    )
    risk = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=True)          # "low"|"medium"|"high"
    excerpt = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=True)       # short summary for list views
    raised_by_phone = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=True)
    confidence = sa.Column(sa.Numeric, nullable=True)

    subject = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)
    body = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)
    # Extended 10-state status (stored as text, validated in service layer)
    status = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False, default="new", server_default="new")
    created_at = sa.Column(
        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
        nullable=False,
        server_default=sa.func.now(),
    )

Now I have the full picture. Let me finalize the review:

### Key findings:

1. **`source` field has no enum constraint** — `source = sa.Column(sa.Text, nullable=False)` — it's a plain text field with no enum. So "letter" and "portal" are valid. PASS.

2. **`status` field** — uses VALID_TICKET_STATUSES for app-layer validation. All seeded statuses ("new", "triaged", "proposed", "completed") are in the valid set. PASS.

3. **Ticket counter `last_num` values** — The counter `last_num=130` for GAR when the highest seeded ticket is GAR-126 creates a 4-number gap. 

The issue here is that new tickets will start at GAR-131 instead of GAR-127, leaving phantom numbers in between. This diverges from the original seed where `last_num` matched the highest ticket exactly, and it could confuse observers wondering where those missing numbers went. The fix is straightforward: align each counter with its highest seeded ticket (GAR-126, BRU-12, LIN-7).

4. **`source="voice"` for t-7835**

The spec calls for "phone" channel for the plumbing leak ticket, and I'm checking whether `source="voice"` is correct. Looking at the existing tickets, voice does map to phone calls, so this checks out.

5. **Confirmation dialog missing Escape key handler**

The dialog in sidebar.tsx doesn't handle the Escape key to close itself, which is a UX gap but not a critical functional issue.

6. **`router.push()` and `router.refresh()` ordering**

After reset, the code navigates to /overview then immediately calls `router.refresh()`, but the refresh might fire against the current page instead of the destination page.  The better approach would be to just use `router.push()` alone or do a hard redirect with `window.location.href`. This could prevent the properties list from reloading properly after reset.

7. **Dialog backdrop doesn't close the dialog**

Clicking outside the dialog has no effect, which is another accessibility gap.

8. **Unused `ContextChunk` import**

This was already in the original code, so it's not something I introduced.

9. **`source="letter"` for t-7843**

The source field accepts plain text values, so "letter" is valid.

10. **Checking `t-7835` source value**

Looking at the seeded ticket data, I'm seeing a pattern of duplicate sources across multiple tickets — several are marked as "voice" for phone calls, multiple use "email", and there's one "portal" entry. The data shows some redundancy in how sources are distributed across the tickets rather than having unique variety.

The acceptance criteria asks for tickets arriving from different sources to demonstrate the multi-channel nature, and while individual tickets do repeat sources, the full set collectively covers all four channels (voice, email, letter, portal), so the requirement is satisfied in spirit.

Now I'm looking at a more critical issue with the `router.push` and `router.refresh()` interaction after a reset. The navigation to the overview page and the server re-fetch are happening concurrently, which could cause timing issues with how the sidebar's properties list gets populated through its `useEffect` hook.

The cleaner solution would be to emit a custom event to trigger the sidebar refresh directly, or use a full browser reload instead. This is medium severity since the reset itself works, but the sidebar might display stale ticket counts until the user navigates elsewhere or the polling cycle refreshes the data.

I'm now ready to compile the final review with the two main issues identified: the `last_num` counter mismatch creating phantom gaps, and the potential race condition with the router navigation and refresh.

The remaining checks all pass — new tickets have valid statuses, source values are correct, idempotency is preserved, the original tickets are unchanged, all foreign key references are valid, context markdown follows the proper hierarchy, and vendor emails are included.

Now I'm looking at the highest severity issue, which is the counter gap. Let me reconsider whether this is actually a bug — the original code set `last_num=120` to match the last ticket number exactly.

The problem is that the last GAR ticket is now GAR-126, but I set `last_num=130`, which means tickets GAR-127 through GAR-130 will never be used as stable seeded tickets, and the next auto-generated ticket will jump to GAR-131. This breaks the established pattern and will confuse demos, so it should be `last_num=126` at minimum.

Both the counter issue and the router.refresh() ordering are self-correcting problems.

message.content:
## Fix Self-Critic Issues

Fix these issues identified in the self-review:

[
  {
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "database",
    "file": "backend/app/services/seed_service.py",
    "line_range": "585-589",
    "description": "Ticket counter last_num values overshoot the highest seeded ticket numbers. The original seed set last_num=120 matching exactly the last seeded GAR ticket (GAR-120). The new highest seeded tickets are GAR-126, BRU-12, and LIN-7, but the counters are set to last_num=130/15/10. This creates phantom gaps: GAR-127 through GAR-130 will never exist, and the next simulate-ticket call will produce GAR-131 instead of GAR-127. This breaks the established numbering convention and will confuse demo observers.",
    "suggested_fix": "Change the counters to match the highest seeded numbers: PropertyTicketCounter(property_id='p1', prefix='GAR', last_num=126), PropertyTicketCounter(property_id='p2', prefix='BRU', last_num=12), PropertyTicketCounter(property_id='p3', prefix='LIN', last_num=7)",
    "auto_fixable": true
  },
  {
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "frontend",
    "file": "frontend/apps/web/components/sidebar.tsx",
    "line_range": "70-73",
    "description": "router.push('/overview') followed immediately by router.refresh() is a race condition. router.refresh() invalidates the Next.js server-component cache for the current route (whichever page the user was on), not for /overview. The sidebar's properties list is fetched via a useEffect that only re-runs on bus events or mount \u2014 after reset it will show stale ticket counts until the user triggers a navigation or the sidebar re-mounts. The confirmation dialog also has no Escape key or backdrop-click handler to dismiss it.",
    "suggested_fix": "Replace router.push('/overview'); router.refresh() with window.location.href = '/overview' for a full page reload that guarantees all client state (sidebar, cached queries) is wiped. Alternatively, dispatch a bus event after reset to trigger the sidebar refresh, then navigate.",
    "auto_fixable": true
  },
  {
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "frontend",
    "file": "frontend/apps/web/components/sidebar.tsx",
    "line_range": "309-341",
    "description": "The confirmation dialog modal has no Escape key handler and clicking the backdrop overlay does not close it. Standard UX convention (and accessibility expectation) is that both actions dismiss the dialog. Currently only the 'Abbrechen' button closes it.",
    "suggested_fix": "Add an onKeyDown handler on the wrapping div that calls setShowResetConfirm(false) when e.key === 'Escape'. Add an onClick handler on the outer backdrop div that closes the dialog, and a stopPropagation on the inner dialog div to prevent click-through.",
    "auto_fixable": true
  },
  {
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "integration",
    "file": "backend/app/services/seed_service.py",
    "line_range": "29",
    "description": "ContextChunk is imported (line 29) but never used directly in seed_service.py \u2014 only create_context_chunks() from context_service is called. This was present in the original file and not introduced by this sprint, but it remains dead code.",
    "suggested_fix": "Remove 'from app.models.context_chunks import ContextChunk' since it is unused.",
    "auto_fixable": true
  }
]

For each fix:
1. Make the code change
2. Commit with format: [ai-builder/self-fix] <description>\nSprint: N | Self-critic fix

Fix ALL issues listed above.

## Final Step (CRITICAL)
After all fixes, run `git status`. If there are ANY uncommitted changes:
```
git add -A
git commit -m "[ai-builder/self-fix] finalize fixes
Sprint: N | Self-critic final"
```
